reason: A is the better-defined and more falsifiable proposal, with a controlled composition change, matched compressive tests at room temperature and ~1000 °C, quantitative acceptance criteria, and at least analogous prior evidence. Its claimed 10% density reduction and strength retention are optimistic—Hf-to-Zr substitution more plausibly gives roughly a 5–7% density decrease and may reduce high-temperature strength—but B is vaguer, unsupported, overstates the likely density decrease, and does not specify a consistent high-temperature mechanical metric.
